_why: Run 20260917-1030 (reverse-proxy): the model's REC bodies describe the live ingress set-up and its weaknesses in detail, and most cite the recorded-incidents section, which is not published. Each claim below is the model's own wording with those clauses cut (marked …), the same cut the public toolsmith repo made in examples/quarantine/. Numbers are unchanged. The Rollback lines are dropped (they map the tunnel topology).

rec-20260917-1030-1.claim:
Incumbent: cloudflared-web ×2 + npmplus + cloudflared-connector on nas — why: … two dead cloudflared-web containers consume 10.9 MB [F012] + 13.3 MB [F013] for zero function; npmplus consumes 119.1 MB RAM and 9.23% CPU … [F014]
Candidate: Keep existing stack; remove dead containers; … decommission NPMplus — source: phase-1 analysis
Licence: npmplus (zoeyvid) — GNU AGPL v3 [source: https://github.com/ZoeyVid/NPMPlus/blob/main/LICENSE]; cloudflared — Apache-2.0 [source: https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/blob/main/LICENSE]
Health: npmplus latest release 2026-07-24-r1 [source: https://github.com/ZoeyVid/NPMPlus/releases]; cloudflared latest tag 2026.9.1 [source: https://hub.docker.com/r/cloudflare/cloudflared/tags]
Resources: npmplus 79 MB compressed Docker image vs target nas rootfs 0 MB free of 1664 MB [F037]; cloudflared 27.4 MB [source: https://hub.docker.com/r/cloudflare/cloudflared/tags]
Sandbox: not tested (no sandbox run this week)
Migration effort: M — decommission two cloudflared-web containers; … shut down npmplus once migrated
Verdict: REJECT — slimming cloudflared-web is a quick win, but without replacing NPMplus the core pains persist; NPMplus should be replaced, not kept.

rec-20260917-1030-2.claim:
Incumbent: npmplus on nas (119.1 MB / 9.23%) + cloudflared-web ×2 — why: dual ingress paths …, nas disk full [F037]
Candidate: Expand Caddy on CT100 to absorb npmplus-proxied vhosts … — source: https://caddyserver.com/features
Licence: Apache-2.0 [source: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/LICENSE] — class: OSI
Health: last release 2026-06-03 (v2.11.4) [source: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases]
Resources: single static Go binary; Alpine Docker image ~23 MB; no external DB or cache; idle memory typically 10–30 MB — source: https://hub.docker.com/_/caddy/tags vs target CT100 free 21300 MB of 37997 MB rootfs and 7116 MB of 8192 MB RAM [F027]
Sandbox: not tested (no sandbox run this week)
Migration effort: M — add NPMplus-hosted vhosts to CT100's Caddyfile; … existing Caddyfile already uses forward_auth …
Verdict: ADOPT-TRIAL — expands what already works, eliminates dual ingress and the nas SPOF in one move, Apache-2.0 licence fits standing preferences [F002][F006], and CT100 has headroom [F027]. Requires manual Caddyfile edits (owner accustomed) and updating tunnel targets; no service discovery needed since the estate is small and static.

rec-20260917-1030-3.claim:
Incumbent: Caddy on CT100 + npmplus on nas — why: same pains as above plus introducing a second proxy adds operational complexity for no gain
Candidate: Replace both proxies with Traefik v3, likely on CT104 (docker host) or CT100 — source: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/features/
Licence: MIT [source: https://github.com/traefik/traefik/blob/master/LICENSE.md] — class: OSI
Health: last release 2026-09-04 (v3.7.13) [source: https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases]
Resources: single Go binary; ~53 MB Docker image; no external DB for basic operation; idle 20–40 MB typical — source: https://hub.docker.com/_/traefik/tags vs target CT104 free 23562 MB rootfs of 60386 MB and 1665 MB RAM [F033][F079] or CT100 free [F027]
Sandbox: not tested (no sandbox run this week)
Migration effort: L — rewrite routing from Caddyfile + NPMplus GUI configs into Traefik dynamic YAML/TOML or Docker labels; new infra dependency; no CF DNS-01 module compiled in (would need configuration)
Verdict: WATCH — Traefik is healthy, well-licenced, and fits the docker-heavy CT104 profile well; however the estate's reverse-proxy topology is small and static …, making Traefik's service-discovery value proposition irrelevant here while its higher migration cost is certain. Revisit if the estate grows significantly beyond its current service count.
